files.content:
# Todo List Application - Requirements Analysis

## 1. Introduction
The Todo List backend service delivers a minimal, production-grade solution for managing task items. Its objective is to enable users to reliably create, view, update, complete, and delete personal todo items with absolute attention to robustness, operational boundaries, and compliance. The focus is to establish a solid foundation for future extensibility while preserving simplicity.

## 2. User Actors & Service Scope

### User Actors
- **End User (Member):** A person with an account who manages their own todos. Can perform all CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations on their own data.
- **Admin:** System administrator with elevated access for regulatory, support, or operational oversight. May access all users’ todos for compliance or support purposes and can execute privileged bulk operations.

### Service Scope
The Todo List application includes only the following required features:
  - Todo item creation, viewing, updating, deletion
  - Completion/incompletion state management
  - Personal and administrative (admin) access levels
  - Bulk operation support (on owned items only; elevated for admin)
  - Data privacy, basic audit, and regulatory compliance support
No advanced/optional features (e.g., notification, collaboration, advanced search) are included in this minimal viable version.

## 3. Functional Requirements (EARS Format)

### Todo Creation (Single and Bulk)
- WHEN a user creates a single todo, THE system SHALL allow input of a title (≤100 characters) and description (≤1,000 characters), both validated. Blanks and invalid entries SHALL be rejected.
- WHEN a user submits a batch creation of todos, THE system SHALL accept up to 50 items per request and reject larger batches with a clear error. IF any item in the batch fails validation, THEN THE system SHALL reject the entire batch and return item-level feedback indicating validation failures.

### Todo Updating
- WHEN a user requests update to their own todo, THE system SHALL validate title and description limits, disallow blank/invalid content, and confirm user ownership. IF the item does not belong to the user or does not exist, THEN THE system SHALL return an access denied or not found error.
- WHEN an admin requests an update, THE system SHALL validate business logic as for a user, but apply update to any item in the system subject to audit logging.
- WHEN a batch update is requested (e.g., to mark multiple todos as done/undone), THE system SHALL allow up to 50 items per operation, apply validations to each item, and reject the whole batch if any fail (as with creation rules).

### Todo Deletion
- WHEN a user requests deletion, THE system SHALL allow deletion of their own todos only, enforcing a maximum of 50 items per batch. If more, reject the request with explanation. Empty deletion requests SHALL be rejected.
- WHEN an admin deletes todos, THE system SHALL permit deletion of any todo, requiring audit trail recording for each operation.

### Todo State Transition
- WHEN a user toggles state (complete/incomplete), THE system SHALL verify ownership and only apply transitions to their own items. Attempted transitions of deleted/archived items SHALL be rejected.
- IF an admin toggles state, THE system SHALL record the action for audit purposes and allow override as required for support.

#### Core Flows (Mermaid)
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Create Todo"] --> B["Validate Title/Description"]
  B -->|"Valid"| C["Save Item"]
  B -->|"Invalid"| D["Reject & Inform User"]
  C --> E["Show Confirmation"]
  D --> F["Cancel/Create Another"]
```

### Todo Retrieval, Listing, and Pagination
- WHEN a user lists their todos, THE system SHALL return only their own items, paginated with a default size of 20 and efficiently supporting up to 1,000 items per user. IF page requested exceeds available data, return an empty set.
- WHEN an admin lists todos, THE system SHALL support full access for compliance monitoring or support, respecting data privacy regulations.

### Error and Validation Handling
- WHEN a request violates field limits, business rule, or ownership, THE system SHALL reject the request and clearly inform the user about the error with actionable feedback.
- WHEN item IDs do not exist, belong to another user, or reference deleted/archived items, THE system SHALL return not found or unauthorized.
- WHEN concurrent actions (edit/delete) occur on the same item, THE system SHALL ensure atomic operation; only the first committed succeeds, later requests fail with error.

### Bulk Operations (General)
- WHEN a bulk operation is initiated, THE system SHALL enforce a maximum batch size of 50. Exceeding batches are rejected with a clear message. For all-or-nothing operation semantics, if any single validation fails, the process is rejected and item-wise feedback must be provided.

#### Bulk Operation Flow (Mermaid)
```mermaid
graph LR
    A["Request Bulk Operation (Create/Update/Delete)"] --> B["Validate Batch Size (≤50)"]
    B -->|"Batch size OK"| C["Validate Each Item"]
    B -->|"Batch too large"| D["Reject with Error"]
    C --> E{"All Items Valid?"}
    E -->|"Yes"| F["Execute Operation"]
    E -->|"No"| G["Reject and Return Item-Level Errors"]
    F --> H["Return Success"]
    D --> I["Return Error Response"]
```

## 4. Non-Functional & Operational Requirements

### Performance
- WHEN the system is under normal usage, THE system SHALL keep error rates below 1%, support up to 100,000 active users, and scale to at least 1,000 todos per user without functional degradation.
- WHEN data volume or operation rate exceeds these, THE system SHALL rate-limit or block excess requests, providing users with context about the restriction and expected reset interval.

### Scalability
- THE system SHALL be designed for easy configuration of user limits, batch sizes, and other operation boundaries without code rewrites.
- WHEN faced with temporary surges (e.g., media coverage), THE system SHALL degrade gracefully by slowing operations/rate-limiting but must not lose or corrupt data.
- All system timestamps SHALL be recorded in Asia/Seoul timezone using ISO 8601 format.

### Reliability & Availability
- THE Todo List SHALL have >99.5% monthly uptime, with robust error handling for user and system failures.

### Data Retention & Auditability
- WHEN a user’s account is deleted, THE system SHALL promptly and permanently remove their todos and personal details, unless retention is legally required. Admin operations SHALL be fully audit-logged, recording actor identity, timestamp, and nature of each change.
- WHEN required by law, THE system SHALL allow users to export their data in a structured format (JSON/CSV).

### Legal/Compliance Requirements
- THE system SHALL store only minimum required personal data, provide audit trails for all admin access, and maintain operational history per current and anticipated regulatory needs, including GDPR-equivalent requirements and data localization if required.

#### Compliance Flow (Mermaid)
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["User Requests Account Deletion"] --> B["Erase Todos & Personal Data"]
  B --> C["Update Audit Log"]
  C --> D{"Retention Needed?"}
  D -->|"Yes"| E["Retain as Required by Law"]
  D -->|"No"| F["Complete Data Removal"]
```

## 5. Special Scenarios & Edge Case Handling

### Empty States
- WHEN a user with no todos accesses the system, THE system SHALL display an empty set with no errors.

### Input Boundary Conditions
- THE system SHALL enforce maximum title (100 characters) and description (1,000 characters) limits, prohibit whitespace-only entries, and must reject any field exceeding these boundaries with specific error description.

### Pagination
- WHEN users have more than 20 items, THE system SHALL paginate results. For requests with out-of-range page numbers, return an empty set without errors.

### Orphaned and Nonexistent Items
- WHEN referencing a non-existent or deleted todo, or one not belonging to the user, THE system SHALL return not found or unauthorized.
- Deleted/archived items cannot be modified except by admin (with full audit trail).

### Concurrent Modification
- WHEN two actions target the same item at the same time, THE system SHALL allow only the first successful one; other(s) receive a conflict error with clear feedback.

### Edge Case Summary Table
| Scenario                                   | System Behavior                                     |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| Empty batch submission                     | Reject with error, notify user                      |
| Exceeding batch size (>50)                 | Reject with error, inform batch size limit          |
| Too long todo title                        | Reject, specify max 100 chars in error              |
| Special character/blank-only title         | Reject if validation fails                          |
| Concurrent requests on same todo           | Only one allowed, remainder error                   |
| Query with no results                      | Return empty set, no error                          |
| Referencing not found/other’s item         | Return not found/unauthorized                       |
| Exceeding pagination parameters            | Return empty list, no error                         |

## 6. Security & Authentication
- WHEN a user interacts with the system, THE system SHALL require authentication for all mutating operations.
- THE system SHALL enforce actor-based access control—non-admins can access/manipulate only their own items.
- Admins MAY perform privileged actions (bulk, cross-user access) only with full audit trail and notifications where appropriate.
- Data privacy standards SHALL apply in all operations; all access, creation, updating, and deletion SHALL be properly authorized.
- WHEN a user requests data export or deletion, THE system SHALL verify identity and intent via secure authentication prior to processing.

## 7. Conclusion
The above requirements provide backend developers with a production-grade, stable, and extensible foundation for a Todo List application, focusing on a minimal, robust set of features. Extensions (such as notifications, collaboration, or analytics) are explicitly out of scope for this version and can be considered in future enhancements.

models.name: todo_list_system_configs
models.description:
System-wide configuration and operational parameters for the Todo List application.

This model stores key-value pairs representing global settings, feature toggles, and core system options that govern application-level behavior. Each configuration is uniquely identified by its key and may store settings such as default timezone, maintenance flags, operational feature gates, or reserved identifiers for system processes.

Configurations in this table are not user- or admin-specific—they apply to the entire deployment and provide a foundation for evolving operational requirements. All updates are tracked with timestamps, and soft deletion is supported for historical audit and safe rotation of system configuration elements.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for the system configuration record.

plainFields.name: key
plainFields.description: Unique configuration key identifying the system setting. Examples include 'default_timezone', 'feature_maintenance_mode', or other core options. Must be unique within this table.

plainFields.name: value
plainFields.description: Configuration value as a string. Can store serialized data for complex options but typically represents a scalar system setting relevant to the business or application.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional detailed description of the purpose and business context for this configuration entry. Useful for documenting intent and supporting operational maintenance.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the configuration entry was created. Used for audit purposes and operational monitoring.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the configuration entry. Enables tracking of modifications for audit and compliance.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp indicating soft deletion of the configuration entry. Used for operational safety and rollback capability.

models.name: todo_list_users
models.description:
Represents registered, authenticated individual end users of the Todo List service.

Each user can create, view, edit, complete, and delete only their own todo items. Users are granted no visibility or control over any other user's account or related data. This table also stores authentication credentials, unique email address, locked status for moderation, and timestamps for account lifecycle.

Audit requirements mandate that all status changes and deletion actions are logged in subsidiary tables. Soft deletion is achieved through the deleted_at column.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address of the user. Used for login and system notifications. Must be unique across all users.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Password hash for secure authentication. Never stores plaintext passwords.

plainFields.name: locked
plainFields.description: Account lock status. True if the user is suspended or blocked by admin for policy or security reasons.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for the most recent update to the user profile or credentials.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user was soft-deleted. Null if active.

models.name: todo_list_user_sessions
models.description:
Tracks active and expired authentication sessions for regular users.

Each session records the user ID, connection details, session creation, and expiration times. Enables audit trails of user activity, tracing access for security, compliance, and privacy enforcement. Sessions are subsidiary and always reference their user owner. No password/token fields are stored here; sessions solely track connection context and lifecycle.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was established.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Connection URL or client origin.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL, if any, for the client establishing the session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session ended or was invalidated.

models.name: todo_list_user_deletion_logs
models.description:
Logs events when user accounts are deleted for audit, compliance, or privacy purposes.

Captures the user deleted, time of action, reason (e.g., GDPR, user request, admin action), and administrative actor if applicable. Used for traceability, regulatory audits, and troubleshooting account lifecycle events. Deletion logs are managed solely by system or admin workflows – users do not interact with this table directly.

plainFields.name: deleted_by_admin_id
plainFields.description: ID of the admin who performed the account deletion. Null if self-deleted. Used for audit when admin initiated.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for deletion (GDPR, user request, admin suspension, etc).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the deletion event occurred.

models.name: todo_list_admins
models.description:
Represents administrators with privileged access to system oversight, user management, and moderation.

Admins can view and manage users and any todo in the system, and can impose status/actions such as account locking or deletion for compliance or support. Authentication credentials, unique email, role flags, lifecycle timestamps, and soft deletion status are included. Only privileged personnel are represented; regular users are never present in this table.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address of the admin for login and notification. Must not overlap normal users.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for secure admin authentication. Plain passwords are never retained.

plainFields.name: locked
plainFields.description: Admin account lock status. True if administrator is currently suspended from system use.

plainFields.name: role
plainFields.description: Administrative role or privilege class (e.g., superadmin, moderator). Determines access boundaries within admin workflows.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Account creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Time of last admin profile or credential update.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for the admin account. Null if admin is active.

models.name: todo_list_admin_sessions
models.description:
Tracks each login session for administrators, providing traceability for privileged access and sensitive actions.

Each record ties to an admin account and logs session metadata including connection IP, access URL, referrer, and timestamps. Sessions support compliance, intrusion detection, and accountability. This table never stores authentication secrets, only session lifecycle information.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: References the admin who owns this session. {@link todo_list_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the admin's session origin.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Access URL or service endpoint for this session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Client's referrer for this session connection.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the admin session began.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Time when the admin session was closed or expired.

models.name: todo_list_admin_deletion_logs
models.description:
Records administrative account deletions for audit fulfillment and policy compliance.

Contains deletion event data: admin whose account was deleted, actor executing the deletion (if different), reason code or explanation, and timestamp. Supports forensic review, compliance, and user/account lifecycle transparency. Entries are generated by system or superadmin operations; never directly manipulated by standard admins.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin whose account was deleted. {@link todo_list_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: deleted_by_admin_id
plainFields.description: ID of the higher privilege admin who performed this deletion, if any. Null if self-deleted.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Narrative or code for the account deletion cause.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp the account was deleted.

models.name: todo_list_todos
models.description:
Business entity representing an individual todo item belonging to a single end-user.

Each row records one actionable task with immutable ownership. Enforces all business rules for title, description, and allowed state transitions (pending, completed, archived). Tracks timestamps for creation, last update, and optional completion. Title validation enforced at creation and update. Foreign key to the user table ensures todos are always associated with a valid owner, but remain private to that user unless reviewed by an admin.

Supports efficient per-user queries and batch actions within the user's scope. No group, tag, or collaborative features are present. Hard deletion applies per requirements. State management compliant with audit and admin access handled via external tables.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each todo item.

foreignFields.name: todo_list_user_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign Key. References the owning user. Must reference an existing user. {@link todo_list_users.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Todo title. Required for creation and update. 1–100 characters, validated for non-whitespace content.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional todo description. Maximum 1000 characters. Can be omitted or set to null on creation/update.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Todo status: permitted values are 'pending', 'completed', or 'archived'. Enforces business lifecycle transitions.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Optional due date in ISO 8601 format. Null if not set. Must not be in the past for creation/update.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for when the todo item was created (stored as UTC). Required for data lifecycle and ordering.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for the last time this todo was updated. Maintains user and admin accountability.

plainFields.name: completed_at
plainFields.description: Optional timestamp for when the todo was marked as completed. Null unless status is 'completed'.

models.name: todo_list_audit_logs
models.description:
Audit log of security-relevant, admin, and business actions across the todo system.

This table records every important operation or event that impacts system security, user privacy, admin oversight, or compliance requirements. Log entries are immutably written for each actionable event: todo create/edit/delete, user/admin login/logout, permission checks, admin moderation, authentication failures, and any sensitive business action.

Each entry references the acting entity (user or admin), affected todo (if applicable), session, and includes rich event and context metadata for compliance, investigations, and business monitoring. The log supports traceability, operational monitoring, security audits, and legal reporting. Entries are never deleted or updated: append-only, supporting strict historical query and forensics.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the audit log entry. Globally unique identifier assigned at insertion, ensuring each record is immutable and traceable.

foreignFields.name: actor_user_id
foreignFields.description: References the user who performed the action, if a user initiated this event. Nullable; use actor_admin_id for admin actions. {@link todo_list_users.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_admin_id
foreignFields.description: References the admin who performed the action, if admin initiated. Nullable; use actor_user_id for user-initiated events. {@link todo_list_admins.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_user_session_id
foreignFields.description: References the user session tied to the action, if event is linked to a user session. Nullable. {@link todo_list_user_sessions.id}.

foreignFields.name: actor_admin_session_id
foreignFields.description: References the admin session if the action was performed during an admin session. Nullable. {@link todo_list_admin_sessions.id}.

foreignFields.name: affected_todo_id
foreignFields.description: References a specific todo if the action/event affects a todo. Nullable for global/auth events not linked to a todo. {@link todo_list_todos.id}.

plainFields.name: event_action
plainFields.description: Describes the action taken or event type (e.g., 'todo_create', 'todo_edit', 'user_login', 'admin_lock_user', 'permission_denied'). Application-defined event type for robust filtering and analytics.

plainFields.name: event_status
plainFields.description: Result status of the event ('success', 'failure', 'denied', etc). Enables filtering audit logs by outcome and error/failure reporting in compliance reviews.

plainFields.name: event_context
plainFields.description: Free-form context data (JSON or string) capturing additional details—affected columns, before/after state, request metadata, error codes. Used for deep auditing, investigation, or legal review. Can be null if event has no extra context.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address of the actor/session generating the event, if available. Nullable.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string (browser/app version) from HTTP request, if captured. Nullable. Supports threat analysis and anomaly detection.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp (UTC) when the audit event was logged. Immutable and required for all records. Used for temporal queries, trending, and compliance timelines.

### `todo_list_system_configs`

System-wide configuration and operational parameters for the Todo List
application.

This model stores key-value pairs representing global settings, feature
toggles, and core system options that govern application-level behavior.
Each configuration is uniquely identified by its key and may store
settings such as default timezone, maintenance flags, operational feature
gates, or reserved identifiers for system processes.

Configurations in this table are not user- or admin-specific—they apply
to the entire deployment and provide a foundation for evolving
operational requirements. All updates are tracked with timestamps, and
soft deletion is supported for historical audit and safe rotation of
system configuration elements.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key for the system configuration record.
- `key`
  > Unique configuration key identifying the system setting. Examples include
  > 'default_timezone', 'feature_maintenance_mode', or other core options.
  > Must be unique within this table.
- `value`
  > Configuration value as a string. Can store serialized data for complex
  > options but typically represents a scalar system setting relevant to the
  > business or application.
- `description`
  > Optional detailed description of the purpose and business context for
  > this configuration entry. Useful for documenting intent and supporting
  > operational maintenance.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the configuration entry was created. Used for audit
  > purposes and operational monitoring.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of the last update to the configuration entry. Enables tracking
  > of modifications for audit and compliance.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp indicating soft deletion of the configuration entry. Used for
  > operational safety and rollback capability.

### `todo_list_users`

Represents registered, authenticated individual end users of the Todo
List service.

Each user can create, view, edit, complete, and delete only their own
todo items. Users are granted no visibility or control over any other
user's account or related data. This table also stores authentication
credentials, unique email address, locked status for moderation, and
timestamps for account lifecycle.

Audit requirements mandate that all status changes and deletion actions
are logged in subsidiary tables. Soft deletion is achieved through the
deleted_at column.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Unique email address of the user. Used for login and system
  > notifications. Must be unique across all users.
- `password_hash`: Password hash for secure authentication. Never stores plaintext passwords.
- `locked`
  > Account lock status. True if the user is suspended or blocked by admin
  > for policy or security reasons.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the user account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for the most recent update to the user profile or credentials.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the user was soft-deleted. Null if active.

### `todo_list_user_sessions`

Tracks active and expired authentication sessions for regular users.

Each session records the user ID, connection details, session creation,
and expiration times. Enables audit trails of user activity, tracing
access for security, compliance, and privacy enforcement. Sessions are
subsidiary and always reference their user owner. No password/token
fields are stored here; sessions solely track connection context and
lifecycle.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_id`: References the associated user. [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users).
- `ip`: IP address from which the session was established.
- `href`: Connection URL or client origin.
- `referrer`: Referrer URL, if any, for the client establishing the session.
- `created_at`: Session creation timestamp.
- `expired_at`: Timestamp when the session ended or was invalidated.

### `todo_list_user_deletion_logs`

Logs events when user accounts are deleted for audit, compliance, or
privacy purposes.

Captures the user deleted, time of action, reason (e.g., GDPR, user
request, admin action), and administrative actor if applicable. Used for
traceability, regulatory audits, and troubleshooting account lifecycle
events. Deletion logs are managed solely by system or admin workflows –
users do not interact with this table directly.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `user_id`: User who was deleted. [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users).
- `deleted_by_admin_id`
  > ID of the admin who performed the account deletion. Null if self-deleted.
  > Used for audit when admin initiated.
- `reason`: Reason for deletion (GDPR, user request, admin suspension, etc).
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the deletion event occurred.

### `todo_list_admins`

Represents administrators with privileged access to system oversight,
user management, and moderation.

Admins can view and manage users and any todo in the system, and can
impose status/actions such as account locking or deletion for compliance
or support. Authentication credentials, unique email, role flags,
lifecycle timestamps, and soft deletion status are included. Only
privileged personnel are represented; regular users are never present in
this table.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Unique email address of the admin for login and notification. Must not
  > overlap normal users.
- `password_hash`
  > Hashed password for secure admin authentication. Plain passwords are
  > never retained.
- `locked`
  > Admin account lock status. True if administrator is currently suspended
  > from system use.
- `role`
  > Administrative role or privilege class (e.g., superadmin, moderator).
  > Determines access boundaries within admin workflows.
- `created_at`: Account creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Time of last admin profile or credential update.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp for the admin account. Null if admin is active.

### `todo_list_admin_sessions`

Tracks each login session for administrators, providing traceability for
privileged access and sensitive actions.

Each record ties to an admin account and logs session metadata including
connection IP, access URL, referrer, and timestamps. Sessions support
compliance, intrusion detection, and accountability. This table never
stores authentication secrets, only session lifecycle information.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `admin_id`: References the admin who owns this session. [todo_list_admins.id](#todo_list_admins).
- `ip`: IP address of the admin's session origin.
- `href`: Access URL or service endpoint for this session.
- `referrer`: Client's referrer for this session connection.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the admin session began.
- `expired_at`: Time when the admin session was closed or expired.

### `todo_list_admin_deletion_logs`

Records administrative account deletions for audit fulfillment and policy
compliance.

Contains deletion event data: admin whose account was deleted, actor
executing the deletion (if different), reason code or explanation, and
timestamp. Supports forensic review, compliance, and user/account
lifecycle transparency. Entries are generated by system or superadmin
operations; never directly manipulated by standard admins.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `admin_id`: Admin whose account was deleted. [todo_list_admins.id](#todo_list_admins).
- `deleted_by_admin_id`
  > ID of the higher privilege admin who performed this deletion, if any.
  > Null if self-deleted.
- `reason`: Narrative or code for the account deletion cause.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp the account was deleted.

### `todo_list_todos`

Business entity representing an individual todo item belonging to a
single end-user.

Each row records one actionable task with immutable ownership. Enforces
all business rules for title, description, and allowed state transitions
(pending, completed, archived). Tracks timestamps for creation, last
update, and optional completion. Title validation enforced at creation
and update. Foreign key to the user table ensures todos are always
associated with a valid owner, but remain private to that user unless
reviewed by an admin.

Supports efficient per-user queries and batch actions within the user's
scope. No group, tag, or collaborative features are present. Hard
deletion applies per requirements. State management compliant with audit
and admin access handled via external tables.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each todo item.
- `todo_list_user_id`
  > Foreign Key. References the owning user. Must reference an existing user.
  > [todo_list_users.id](#todo_list_users).
- `title`
  > Todo title. Required for creation and update. 1–100 characters, validated
  > for non-whitespace content.
- `description`
  > Optional todo description. Maximum 1000 characters. Can be omitted or set
  > to null on creation/update.
- `status`
  > Todo status: permitted values are 'pending', 'completed', or 'archived'.
  > Enforces business lifecycle transitions.
- `due_date`
  > Optional due date in ISO 8601 format. Null if not set. Must not be in the
  > past for creation/update.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp for when the todo item was created (stored as UTC). Required
  > for data lifecycle and ordering.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp for the last time this todo was updated. Maintains user and
  > admin accountability.
- `completed_at`
  > Optional timestamp for when the todo was marked as completed. Null unless
  > status is 'completed'.

### `todo_list_audit_logs`

Audit log of security-relevant, admin, and business actions across the
todo system.

This table records every important operation or event that impacts system
security, user privacy, admin oversight, or compliance requirements. Log
entries are immutably written for each actionable event: todo
create/edit/delete, user/admin login/logout, permission checks, admin
moderation, authentication failures, and any sensitive business action.

Each entry references the acting entity (user or admin), affected todo
(if applicable), session, and includes rich event and context metadata
for compliance, investigations, and business monitoring. The log supports
traceability, operational monitoring, security audits, and legal
reporting. Entries are never deleted or updated: append-only, supporting
strict historical query and forensics.

Properties as follows:

- `id`
  > Primary key for the audit log entry. Globally unique identifier assigned
  > at insertion, ensuring each record is immutable and traceable.
- `actor_user_id`
  > References the user who performed the action, if a user initiated this
  > event. Nullable; use actor_admin_id for admin actions. {@link
  > todo_list_users.id}.
- `actor_admin_id`
  > References the admin who performed the action, if admin initiated.
  > Nullable; use actor_user_id for user-initiated events. {@link
  > todo_list_admins.id}.
- `actor_user_session_id`
  > References the user session tied to the action, if event is linked to a
  > user session. Nullable. [todo_list_user_sessions.id](#todo_list_user_sessions).
- `actor_admin_session_id`
  > References the admin session if the action was performed during an admin
  > session. Nullable. [todo_list_admin_sessions.id](#todo_list_admin_sessions).
- `affected_todo_id`
  > References a specific todo if the action/event affects a todo. Nullable
  > for global/auth events not linked to a todo. [todo_list_todos.id](#todo_list_todos).
- `event_action`
  > Describes the action taken or event type (e.g., 'todo_create',
  > 'todo_edit', 'user_login', 'admin_lock_user', 'permission_denied').
  > Application-defined event type for robust filtering and analytics.
- `event_status`
  > Result status of the event ('success', 'failure', 'denied', etc). Enables
  > filtering audit logs by outcome and error/failure reporting in compliance
  > reviews.
- `event_context`
  > Free-form context data (JSON or string) capturing additional
  > details—affected columns, before/after state, request metadata, error
  > codes. Used for deep auditing, investigation, or legal review. Can be
  > null if event has no extra context.
- `ip_address`
  > IP address of the actor/session generating the event, if available.
  > Nullable.
- `user_agent`
  > User agent string (browser/app version) from HTTP request, if captured.
  > Nullable. Supports threat analysis and anomaly detection.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp (UTC) when the audit event was logged. Immutable and required
  > for all records. Used for temporal queries, trending, and compliance
  > timelines.

operations.specification:
This operation enables new users to register themselves in the Todo List service. It creates a new todo_list_users record, assigning values for essential authentication fields (such as username, email, and password as defined in the schema). The endpoint is open to any unauthenticated client, as registration is a public operation. Only fields explicitly defined in the todo_list_users schema are supported; all custom validation and constraints are enforced according to that structure. Upon successful account creation, a new session may be instantiated using the user sessions model.

Security is enforced by validating required registration fields, such as password complexity and unique email/username constraints as defined. No privilege escalation is possible, since created accounts are regular users by default. All registration attempts must comply with the business rules declared for todo_list_users.

The operation does not grant access to any system or admin capabilities—each user is isolated and unable to interact with other users' records. Business logic for onboarding flows (such as welcome messages or initial configs) is handled in application layers according to requirements.

This registration is a critical prerequisite for all subsequent authentication and authorization actions for end users. Any future changes to join requirements must be reflected in the todo_list_users schema and corresponding registration rules.

Testing for this operation should cover successful registrations, duplicate key rejection, and mandatory field validation according to the schema and project requirements.

Enforces unique and required field constraints from the todo_list_users schema. Registration is public, does not confer admin or privileged access, and is a necessary prerequisite for login and all user authorization flows. All onboarding and field validation rules are strictly enforced as described in the table definition.

operations.specification:
This operation authenticates an existing user by validating supplied credentials (such as username/email and password), as specified in the todo_list_users schema. It is a public endpoint accessible to any unauthenticated client. Login is only permitted for accounts that exist in the users table, and valid credentials must match the stored hashes or authentication data as implemented in the service layer.

The endpoint checks only credentials corresponding to fields present in todo_list_users. No cross-user or admin logins are permitted through this operation; it strictly issues JWT tokens for normal end users upon correct authentication.

Upon successful authentication, access and refresh tokens following the configured scheme are returned—structured as ITodoListUser.IAuthorized. No sensitive credential information is exposed in the response. All password policy and failed attempt tracking are handled per business and security requirement documents.

Security is maintained by enforcing account lock rules, logging suspicious activity, and rejecting invalid authentication attempts according to the todo_list_users schema and system policy.

This login is a prerequisite for all actions that require authentication. The operation's test suite should ensure correct failure responses for invalid users, locked accounts, and incorrect passwords, as well as successful login cases and full compliance with password security and token issuance rules.

Only normal todo_list_users accounts are supported—admins must use their own login endpoint. Security and credential validation correspond to the todo_list_users schema and defined business rules. Operation supports only those fields and policies present in the schema.

operations.specification:
This operation refreshes user JWT tokens using a valid refresh token previously issued to the authenticated user. The refresh token must comply with service security policy as defined by business requirements. The endpoint is public in that it requires no existing session, but a valid refresh token must be supplied (generally as part of request data).

It is designed to extend authenticated sessions for users of the todo_list_users table. The actual refresh logic strictly follows the token lifecycle and validation constraints from requirements and system design documents, and the operation enforces checks against revoked, expired, or tampered tokens.

This endpoint does not permit privilege escalation, nor does it grant any new access rights beyond those already assigned to the user by their previous login. Upon success, a new pair of access and refresh tokens in ITodoListUser.IAuthorized format is returned. Failed refreshes result in strict error responses as documented in requirements.

Security logic is implemented at the service layer and references all relevant constraints defined for JWT/refresh flows by the backend and requirements files.

Testing for this operation must cover valid refreshes, invalid or expired token rejection, and edge scenarios per requirements documents.

Only valid, untampered tokens are accepted, following all refresh lifecycle constraints. The operation supports only user-level refresh—no admin or cross-account tokens are accepted.

operations.specification: This operation allows a new administrator to register (join) the system. It takes a unique email and password, hashes the password for secure storage, and creates a corresponding entry in the todo_list_admins table. The operation issues a JWT token pair to the new admin upon successful registration. The todo_list_admins schema enforces unique email addresses and ensures passwords are never stored in plain text (password_hash field is used for storage). Account creation timestamps and the default admin locked status are also set. This operation is only available to unauthenticated (public) users for onboarding new admins. The associated table is todo_list_admins.
operations.description:
This endpoint registers a new admin by creating a record in todo_list_admins. The required fields include a unique email address (enforced by the unique index on email) and a password, which is stored securely as a hashed value in the password_hash field, never in plain text. Upon registration, the admin's account lock status is set as appropriate, and a creation timestamp is recorded in created_at.

Password security is enforced at both the API and database layers; passwords are subjected to policy validation and then securely hashed before being persisted. Email uniqueness is validated against the unique index, and the API returns an error if a duplicate is detected.

Admins have the highest system privileges, and their registration triggers audit logging in down-stream flows (not in this operation directly). This operation does not allow setting the admin's role field or locked status directly; these are handled by system rules or subsequent administrative operations.

The response for a successful operation includes newly issued authentication tokens (access and refresh) as documented by ITodoListAdmin.IAuthorized, aligning with JWT-based onboarding procedures. On error or conflict, a suitable response is provided.

Related operations include /auth/admin/login for subsequent authentication and /auth/admin/refresh for token renewal. Audit and logging are recommended by the business rules but are not performed in this operation.

requestBody.description: Registration details for new admin, including email and password.

responseBody.description: Authenticated admin token information as per ITodoListAdmin.IAuthorized DTO.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: This operation enables a registered admin to log in. The admin provides their email and password, which are checked against the todo_list_admins table. On successful authentication, password_hash is compared using a secure hash validation algorithm; if the account is not locked and hasn't been soft-deleted (deleted_at is null), the system issues a JWT token pair. The operation only supports logins for email addresses present in todo_list_admins and respects account lock status. This operation is directly tied to todo_list_admins.
operations.description:
This endpoint authenticates a registered administrator based on their email (unique index in todo_list_admins) and password (hashed, compared securely). If credentials match (verified against password_hash), and the account is not locked (locked is false) or deleted (deleted_at is null), an access and refresh token pair are returned (ITodoListAdmin.IAuthorized DTO). Lock status is checked, and the operation is denied if locked is true, enforcing compliance and incident handling measures.

Authentication failures (bad credentials, locked accounts, or soft-deleted admins) are securely handled and return generic authentication errors to avoid leaking sensitive information. The operation does not permit login for any admin that has been soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null) or is currently locked.

Detailed audit logging is assumed for all login attempts (not implemented in this endpoint directly), supporting system-level traceability of privileged access.

Security is reinforced by requiring password_hash validation and not storing/revealing actual passwords, as per schema best practices. Related operations include /auth/admin/join for onboarding new admins and /auth/admin/refresh for token renewal.

Error handling ensures that locked or deleted accounts are not accessible, and the endpoint returns only minimal error messages for failed logins.
operations.summary: Authenticate a todo_list_admin and issue JWT tokens if successful.

requestBody.description: Admin login credentials: email and password.

responseBody.description: Authenticated admin JWT token information.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: This operation allows an authenticated admin to renew their JWT access and refresh tokens using a valid refresh token. The process verifies the provided refresh token against session and admin state in the todo_list_admins table, confirms the admin account is not locked or soft-deleted, and then issues a fresh token pair. The operation defends against token reuse and account state changes (e.g., locking or deletion since last login). The associated table is todo_list_admins.
operations.description:
This endpoint refreshes authentication tokens for an admin. Token renewal is performed if the refresh token is valid, the associated admin record is still active (deleted_at is null), and the account is not locked (locked is false). Underlying logic ensures that admins who have since been locked or soft-deleted cannot use this operation.

The refresh token is securely validated, potentially against a session store, but always checked to confirm the admin's existence and current status in todo_list_admins. Business logic re-issues access and refresh tokens only if conditions are met; otherwise, appropriate errors are returned. No authentication is performed via password; only the provided refresh token is checked per ITodoListAdmin.IRefresh DTO contracts.

This strengthens session management by ensuring token renewal cannot bypass admin-level restrictions (locked/deleted). The operation does not support role elevation or privilege changes—tokens are renewed at the existing privilege level.

Related admin operations include /auth/admin/login for initial authentication and /auth/admin/join for new registrations. Audit logging is recommended for token refresh attempts but is outside this endpoint's direct scope.

Security concerns are addressed by denying renewal for locked or deleted admins, with detailed error reporting suppressed to prevent information leaks.

responseBody.description: Newly issued JWT token information for admin session.

This operation does not allow setting the admin's role field or locked status directly; these are handled by system rules or subsequent administrative operations.

Authentication failures (bad credentials, locked accounts, or soft-deleted admins) are securely handled and return generic authentication errors to avoid leaking sensitive information. Security is reinforced by requiring password_hash validation and not storing/revealing actual passwords, as per schema best practices. Related operations include /auth/admin/join for onboarding new admins and /auth/admin/refresh for token renewal.
